newsitem.title: CHINA: HK gold ends steeply down on long liquidation.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends steeply down on long liquidation.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold continued its downward spiral on Friday, ending below New York's previous close as physical buying was steamrollered by long liquidation, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$324.60/325.10 per ounce on Friday compared to New York's close at US$325.00/50 on Thursday.
"There was quite a lot of long liquidation," said one local trader.
But dealers said although gold briefly touched a low of $323.50, it bounced back rapidly, leading them to expect upside potential.
"The market overreacted to the Australian gold sales," said one source.
Physical demand had picked up on attractive prices, with one major supplier in the territory describing demand as "heavy".
Some sources said low prices were good for jewellery houses.
"The wave could stop at a lower level and after $320 per ounce, there is no barrier, but nearby (psychological levels are) $321.50 and next at $316.50 per ounce," a senior dealer said.
Hong Kong tael gold also took a beating in intra-day trade, ending HK$72 down at HK$3,006 per tael.

The lowest recorded price in the past four years was seen on March 14, 1993, where local gold dipped to HK$3,018 per tael, equivalent to $327.20 per ounce, an official at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society said.
Hong Kong tael gold has touched well below HK$3,000 per tael. On February 26, 1985, the price of local gold was HK$2,649, or the equivalent of $287.20 per ounce, the official said.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at -6.00.
